transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because things got a bit out of hand recently. I took on this project for the historical society, and... well, I acted like I could run the whole fundraiser all by myself. I just started diving into it—starting all these new quilt designs, calling up volunteers, making schedules, and promising deadlines that I just couldn't possibly meet. It all just caught up with me, I suppose.
Did this period of high energy and activity cause significant problems in your work or social life, or did it land you in the hospital?

I didn't go to the hospital, no. But it definitely caused problems. My husband has actually had to take over all our normal household routines lately. He even had to be the one to deal with the historical society for me, because I... well, I just stopped keeping my commitments. After all those promises I made, I just couldn't face the people who were waiting on me.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling unusually energized or productive in the past, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Um, I don't really think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good and got a lot done around the house, but... no, I haven't ever experienced a period quite like this one. As far as I can remember, this is the first time I've felt that unusually energized, where it just completely took over like that.
Now that this period of high energy has passed, how have you been feeling lately in terms of your mood and your interest in doing things you usually enjoy?

Honestly, my mood has been pretty low. And as for doing things I usually enjoy... well, I used to love checking on my garden, and I always enjoyed working on my own quilt entries. But lately... I don't know, I just look at the fabric and the seed catalogs sitting on the table, and I feel nothing much at all. I just don't have any interest in them right now.
How long have you been feeling this low and losing interest in your hobbies?
It's been about nine months now. Ever since I fell behind on all those quilt orders and the conflicts with the historical society volunteers blew up... I've just been stuck in this low, guilty place.

Before this nine-month period you are currently in, have you ever experienced another time in your life where you felt this low, lost interest in your hobbies, and struggled to function for at least two weeks?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt a little down, but... nothing like this. This is the first time I've been stuck in a rut this deep, for this long.
Over these past nine months, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns, such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual?

Well, my sleep has definitely changed. Back when I was doing all that sewing and making those phone calls, I was only sleeping a few hours a night and I'd wake up ready to go. But now... it's completely different. Most nights I just lie awake worrying about everything. Or, if I do finally fall asleep, I end up sleeping really late into the morning, and I still feel completely worn out when I get up.
During that period where you were working so intensely and sleeping very little, did you ever feel like you had special powers, or did you ever see or hear things that others around you did not?

No, I never felt like I had any sort of special powers or anything like that. I was just really focused and felt like I could get a lot done. And I definitely haven't seen or heard anything that wasn't there. It was just a lot of energy, that's all.
Over these past nine months, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight?
No, not really. I mean, I guess I eat about the same as I usually do. My weight hasn't really gone up or down that I've noticed. I just don't have the energy to cook much, but I'm still eating.
During these past nine months, have you felt physically slowed down, like your movements or speech are sluggish, or have you felt restless and unable to sit still?

Well, it's been both, I guess. My husband actually pointed it out. Back when I was doing all that sewing, he said I was just pacing around the room constantly, sorting the same piles of fabric over and over again like I couldn't stop moving. But now... it's the opposite. Some mornings I move so slowly that just getting up to make a pot of coffee feels like a massive chore. Everything just feels heavy and sluggish now.
Looking back at that time when you were sleeping very little and working intensely on the quilts and the fundraiser, how many days in a row did that high-energy period last?

It was a lot more than a few days, actually. That whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project... I'd say it went on for about five months. Yeah, about five months straight before everything just kind of fell apart.
